notes:
Lead background: small D2C e-comm platform (headless storefront + chat support). Came in via webinar + community post. Trialled hosted API for: 1) customer support assistant (summaries + resolutions), 2) recommendations / related-products endpoint. Initial onboarding: created API key, ran smoke tests.
Stalled behaviour: low usage after initial key exchange — only a couple of evaluation calls. Customer quote from 1/14: "Looks promising but need a clearer cost story vs what we're already running." Switched to parallel PoC with Anthropic embeddings on 1/30 "to test vector quality and pricing".
Technical notes (from SE call 1/18): prefix caching would help their chat workflow, batching not yet implemented in their client. Observed latency spikes around 200ms for short prompts; larger >1k token tests had cost concerns. They asked whether Redwood has auto-fallback model routing if regional capacity is constrained — SE clarified hosted API supports simple fallback but requested doc link (sent).
Security / procurement: submitted SSO/SAML and audit log questions; SMB but still needs basic controls for audit trail. Not requesting on-prem or VPC.
Commercial: price-sensitive; will likely choose lowest cost-per-inference unless convinced on reliability/observability. Interested in a short-term promo or trial extension tied to usage metrics.
AE notes / recommended playbook: 1) Send one-pager comparing token pricing + observed latency vs Anthropic/OpenAI on common payloads (include our observed sample results). 2) Offer 30% off for first month or extended credits if they run defined migration tests. 3) Quick SE pairing session to add basic batching + prefix cache examples (30-45m). 4) Provide security FAQ link and quick SSO checklist.
Current tone: lukewarm but salvageable. Key risk: competitor PoC is cheaper in their early runs; risk of churn high if we don't get them to run migration benchmarks within 2 weeks.
summary: SMB inbound from webinar; early evaluation but low usage after initial key. Main risks: competitor PoC, pricing sensitivity, minor technical friction. Next: targeted pricing comparison + SE pairing session.
